strategy.summary: Gleitring-Systeme Kaltenbrunn AG is a sound, group-owned Swiss seal maker and our single approved source for the ATEX, drinking-water approved cartridge seal part:340012. It owns the tooling and has just extended its approvals. Its delivery and quality records are excellent. We are a small customer to it. Head office has frozen all price reductions until December 2027, and changes above a threshold need a pricing committee that meets every two weeks. The price has been flat since 2023. Its renewal asks have shrunk each year and always settled at zero. The contract auto-renewed for 2027, and no price-change notice is on record. Room for a cut is small. The realistic win is to hold the current price for longer, ideally 24 months during its freeze, and take value through terms: payment days, binding volume backed by the rising forecast, and steadier call-offs. Evidence on persona is thin: two meeting notes and one e-mail.
strategy.decision_maker: Sales director (stated the head-office freeze and openness on payment and call-off terms). The key account manager handles day-to-day talks and can decide small moves. Larger price changes go to their pricing committee, which meets every two weeks.

persona.style: Cordial and relationship-oriented, policy-bound on price; negotiates within head-office rules and is open on non-price terms
other_traits: single source with supplier-owned tooling and freshly extended drinking-water approvals
we are a small customer to it
soft renewal asks, historically settled at zero

needs.detail: Binding volume and smoother call-offs. Our forecast rises and is uneven month to month; we also generate rush and changed orders.
Head office forbids reductions until end-2027; it wants to keep the current price and recover modest labour and rubber inflation.
Higher forecast volume is shared with them and is worth more to them when bound.
Top delivery and zero-defect record; it values being treated as a reference partner.
Short payment terms are already in its favour versus our standard. It is open on payment terms but shows no financial stress, so cash need is weak.

constraints.detail: Head-office freeze on all price reductions until December 2027.
Price changes above the threshold need the pricing committee, which meets every two weeks. This slows any round that asks for a larger move.
Only approved source with full quota; it owns the tooling; approvals were extended recently. Switching is costly and slow.
Prices are fixed per calendar year with a notice requirement. The contract auto-renewed, and no notice for a 2027 change appears in the records. This binds them more than us.

levers.why: Strongest trade asset. Rising, shared forecast to bind in exchange for a long price hold or better terms.
Notice period for a 2027 change appears missed; it neutralises any increase ask on contract grounds without confrontation.
Their own stated openness on payment and call-off flexibility; it frames the trade route they already accepted.
Three renewals settled at zero; anchors a zero-increase outcome.
Shows margin to absorb modest labour and rubber drivers. Use it to resist an increase, not to demand a cut under the freeze.
We are a reliable payer; supports a payment-term trade and fairness framing.
Current orders anchor the price; a fresh filler record for a later round.
Stable price history as a late fresh fact.

trades.why: Lock the current price for 24 months, covering their freeze period; length is valued by them and gives us cover against driver inflation.
Bind volume in line with the rising forecast, within our real need, for price hold or a small step.
Net 30 already favours them. Keep it as a give in exchange for price, or test a longer term only if offered cheaply. Do not demand long payment plus a cut under the freeze.
Their standard lead time works; asking shorter would be priced up.
Fixed price is better for us while labour and rubber rise; avoid a clause unless they insist, and then price it carefully.
If an increase becomes unavoidable, delay it to the end of the freeze period rather than concede early.

price_view.reasoning: Should-cost suggests a healthy but not excessive margin with a wide error band. Labour and rubber drivers are rising and mildly support the flat price. A head-office freeze blocks reductions. History shows we can hold at zero increase reliably. Realistic outcome: current price held for longer, with value via volume, length and terms. A cut is possible only as a small step bought with binding volume plus length, and may wait for the committee.

do: Acknowledge their delivery and zero-defect performance and the extended approvals
Frame proposals as partnership and planning security
Put the full term package in the first e-mail (length, binding volume, payment position, strongest record)
Keep moves within what the key account manager can approve where possible, to avoid committee delays
dont: Do not demand a price reduction head-on against the freeze
Do not threaten resourcing or bluff alternatives; there is no approved second source
Do not ask for long payment plus a price cut together
Do not cite copper, electronics, steel or power news as about this supplier

traps: Pushing for a cut after they say prices are frozen leads to hold and then a final offer; they move once
Threatening to switch is not credible given single source, tooling and approvals
Using performance (delivery, quality) against them: their record is spotless and it costs credibility
Citing the power-price fall: they will dismiss it, and the energy share is unknown
Committing volume beyond real need just for a small step
Asking for shorter lead time or tighter quality terms they would price up
Re-citing a record already used in the same case
Countering below a declared final offer
strategy.writer_notes: Open warmly, recognise their reliability and the approval extension. Propose a longer fixed-price hold with binding volume reflecting our rising forecast and steadier, forecast-based call-offs. Note that prices are fixed per calendar year under the contract and that no change notice was received. Invite their alternative for how payment or call-off terms could reflect in price. Expect a single counter; after a hold, close or pursue only the term alternatives they name. Keep any price ask small enough to avoid the pricing committee where possible.
questions_to_ask: Which term combination would help your planning most: longer commitment, binding volume or a fixed call-off schedule?
Does the price freeze also leave room for value through payment or call-off terms, and how would you reflect those?
Would a forecast-based monthly call-off plan reduce your effort on rush orders?
Can the sales director decide on payment and call-off terms directly, or do these also go to the committee?

findings.text: Price EUR 319.11 sits +16.6% above our bottom-up should-cost of EUR 273.72 (material 38.32, conversion 164.78, overhead 70.62, no margin). That is a gross margin of about 14% of price, healthy rather than excessive for a single-source ATEX/drinking-water cartridge seal. Confidence is only ±5% on the estimate, so the true margin may lie between roughly 11% and 21%.
The price has been flat at EUR 319.11 from 2023 through 2026. The current quote repeats it, with no increase asked. The supplier's history: asked +2.3% on average at renewals and settled 0%.

Cost drivers moved up modestly. Labour (LCI-C, weight 0.31) is +2.7% over 12 months and sits at its 36-month peak. Rubber products (PPI-C2219, weight 0.11) are +3.9% and also at peak. The weighted effect is about +1.25% on price. Over the three frozen years the drivers rose more: labour is +10.9% from its 36-month low and rubber +5.5%, so in real terms its margin has eroded. The drivers do not support a price cut now; they mildly support the flat price.

Material is only about 14% of should-cost, so the large market moves in the news (copper +48%, electronics +41%, steel +7.3%) are largely irrelevant to this part. The supplier would struggle to use them credibly. Industrial power at -43% vs 2022 is a minor counter-argument, since energy sits in conversion but its weight is unknown.

Room on price is small. A price reduction is blocked by a head-office freeze until December 2027, and any change above 2% needs their pricing committee. The realistic economic target is to hold EUR 319.11 for longer (multi-year) and seek value through payment terms (30 to 60 days) and volume. The supplier says it is open on payment and call-off flexibility, and forecast volume rises from 1334 to 1598.
Evidence is thin: there is one part, no competing quotes or RFQ, and the should-cost has ±5% error.

Recognition of rising labour and rubber costs

findings.text: Head office has frozen all price reductions until December 2027 (sales director, Aug 2026). A direct price-cut ask will hit a policy wall above the negotiators' heads. They signalled openness on payment terms and call-off flexibility instead, so value must come through trades, not price.

Approval ladder: price changes above 2 % need their pricing committee, which meets every two weeks. Moves under 2 % can be decided by the key account manager. Larger moves add 2-week delays per round. This also applies to any increase they seek.

The supplier is financially sound and we matter little to it. It is a group-owned AG founded in 1946 with 900 staff and EUR 247 M turnover, equity ratio 35.7 % and a stable credit index of 162 (no stress). Our spend is about 0.2 % of its turnover. It can afford to walk away, so pressure tactics are risky.

Its position is strong on part 340012. It is our single approved source with 100 % quota, owns the tooling, and has just extended its drinking-water approvals. Its delivery record (95.8 % on time) and quality record (0 ppm) are excellent, which leaves no performance lever.

Weaknesses on their side are mainly historical. The price has been flat at 319.11 since 2023 while our should-cost estimate is about 16.6 % below it. At past renewals they asked for increases (about +2.3 % on average) but settled at 0 %. Their asks are soft, which helps us resist increases more than it helps win cuts.

Their likely need is cash and planning certainty. The contract is net 30 against our 60-day standard, so they already benefit from short terms. We pay reliably: on average 0.7 days late and never more than 5 days late. Their openness on payment terms suggests faster payment or call-off flexibility can be traded. The contract auto-renewed for 2027.
Their tone is cordial and relationship-oriented (they sent a trade fair invitation). There is little written evidence of their style beyond two meeting notes, so the persona evidence is thin.

findings.text: Framework agreement ctr:4600070420 covers only part:340012 (cartridge seal HI 45 mm, ATEX, drinking-water). It runs 2024-01-01 to 2026-12-31 and extends 12 months unless terminated with 180 days' notice. The termination date (2026-07-04) has passed, so the contract renews automatically to 2027-12-31.

Prices are fixed per calendar year. Any change needs written notice at least 180 days before year end, i.e. by about 2026-07-04 for 2027. No such notice appears in the evidence. If none was given, the 2027 price stays at EUR 319.11 and any increase request can be rejected on contract grounds. This should be verified.

Commercial terms are payment 30 days net (our standard is 60, so this favours them), DAP, and a 56-day lead time. The quality agreement sets a 95% on-time target and a EUR 150 flat fee per complaint. The supplier meets these comfortably: 95.8% on time and 0 ppm.

History: three renewals asked for +3.3%, +2.2% and +1.3% and every one settled at 0%. The price has stayed at EUR 319.11 since 2023 and has never fallen. Their asks are shrinking and they have always accepted zero.

Dependency is asymmetric. On the supplier side:
- It is our single source with a 100% quota, approved since 2019.
- It holds ATEX and drinking-water approvals, recently extended.
- It reportedly owns the tooling.
On our side, we are about 0.2% of its turnover, and it is financially sound. Our leverage rests on the contract and history, not on alternatives.

Call notes: price changes above 2% need their pricing committee, which meets every two weeks. Head office has frozen price reductions until 12/2027. They are open on payment terms and call-off flexibility, so price-down attempts are unlikely; trades should run through payment and volume.

risks: Single source with no RFQ alternative; requalification is costly due to ATEX and drinking-water approvals plus tooling
A hard push for reductions conflicts with their head-office freeze and could sour a 0-ppm supplier
Our late payments (65.7% slightly late) weaken any request for longer payment days

useful_arguments.why: Annual fixed price with 180-day notice blocks a 2027 increase if they gave no notice.
They have settled at 0% three times.
The price has been stable since 2023, which anchors a zero increase.
Anchors the current price at EUR 319.11.
The price is 16.6% above should-cost, so there is margin to absorb cost drivers.
About 20% more volume is a trade asset.
They are open on payment and call-off terms, which gives room for trades.

findings.text: Delivery is excellent and stable: rolling OTD 95.8-100% over nine scorecards (latest 95.8%, target 95%, peers' median 84.6%), class A green throughout. In the last 12 months there were no late receipts; the one miss was an early delivery (4.2% early). Late delivery costs us practically nothing. This argues its case, not ours.

Quality is flawless: 0 ppm, 0 QNs and no overdue 8D reports across all scorecards (peers' median 457 ppm), on about 1,334 pcs a year. The defect cost and chargeback exposure (EUR 150 per complaint) are nil. A ppm or chargeback term costs it nothing to accept but is worth little to us.

Our volume outlook is rising. The forecast for the next 12 months is 1,598 pcs, against 1,334 ordered in the last 12 months (+19.8%). The forecast has risen steadily since 2025-06 (1,259 → 1,469 → 1,458 → 1,598) and is shared with the supplier. This is our main performance-side lever: a binding higher annual volume and a longer commitment in exchange for price or terms.

The price has been flat at EUR 319.11 since the first order in 2023-10, across about 3,934 pcs. The latest POs in 2026-09 are still at 319.11, which anchors against any increase. The supplier has never cut its price despite rising volume and its perfect cost-of-quality record.

We create some friction on our side: 6 rush lines and 6 changed lines out of 72, including a rush PO in 2026-09. Every PO was confirmed on the requested date. Call-off flexibility is something the supplier already gives us. Asking it to absorb more rushes is a cost to it; offering steadier, forecast-based call-offs could be a give from us.
The monthly forecast is uneven: troughs of 92 pcs in 2026-12 and 66 pcs in 2027-08, with peaks of 170 pcs. Committing a schedule helps its capacity planning.

arguments.text: Our price has been held flat at EUR 319.11 since January 2023. That is four calendar years with zero increase, even though we asked for 3.3 %, 2.2 % and 1.3 % at the renewals and each time accepted 0. In real terms we have already given you a reduction of roughly 8-10 %, so a further cut is not reasonable.

Our cost drivers are rising, not falling. Labour cost is up 2.7 % year on year and sits at its 36-month peak. Rubber products are up 3.9 % and also at their peak. Stainless 1.4404, which goes into the cartridge hardware, carries a surcharge 6 % higher than a year ago.

Our performance is reference level. Over the last 12 months we delivered 0 ppm with zero complaints on more than 1,300 pieces, kept on-time delivery at or above the 95 % target throughout, and posted no late receipts in that period. A price cut that puts this service level at risk is not in Hollerau's interest.
Head office has frozen all price reductions until December 2027. I cannot offer a reduction even if I wanted to, and that is consistent with what our sales director told you in August.

This is a niche part, ATEX and drinking-water approved, and we have just invested to extend those approvals to further markets. That certification and approval upkeep is real cost and real value for you.

Your demand pattern costs us money. Your forecast swings from 66 to 170 pieces per month, and there have been 6 rush orders and 6 changed lines. Absorbing that flexibility at an unchanged price is already a concession.

weak_points: We sent no 180-day price-change notice for 2027 and the contract auto-renewed. Strictly, I cannot claim an increase for 2027.
Their should-cost of EUR 273.72 excludes margin. Our price leaves about 14 % on top, which is comfortable, although their confidence in that estimate is only 5 %.
Industrial power is down 43 % on 2022, and energy matters in our machining and sintering.
Material is only about EUR 38 of the cost, so the steel and copper headlines carry limited weight.
The freeze is on reductions, but our own renewal asks have shrunk every year and always ended at 0. That signals we accept flat pricing.
Their volume is growing about 20 %, and we are financially healthy (equity ratio 35.7 %, stable credit index), so we cannot plead hardship.
Their payment term of 30 days is already short in our favour.
Our on-time delivery has dipped to 95.8 %, just at the target.
wants: A binding annual volume of around 1,500-1,600 pieces with a smoother call-off schedule and fewer rushes.
A longer contract of 24-36 months at the current price.
Keeping 30 days payment or shorter; I could trade a small cash discount for 14 days.
An index clause on labour and rubber from 2028 instead of a fixed price.
Staying sole source with 100 % quota and recognition as a preferred supplier.
Possibly a small reduction of no more than 1-2 %, bought only with binding volume plus length, effective no earlier than January 2028 and subject to committee approval.
red_lines: No price reduction effective before January 2028 (head-office freeze).
No extension of payment terms beyond 45 days without a price offset.
No ppm commitment or chargeback above the current EUR 150 flat fee without compensation.
No binding lead time below 56 days for unsmoothed call-offs.
No cut that takes the price below roughly EUR 300.
red_team.opening: Thank Hollerau for a strong partnership and point to 0 ppm and on-time delivery at or above target. Confirm the quote at an unchanged EUR 319.11 and note this is the fourth year without an increase despite rising labour, rubber and stainless costs. State that reductions are not possible under the head-office directive until end-2027. Then offer a constructive path: hold the price fixed through 2028 in exchange for a binding 1,550-piece annual volume and a smoothed monthly call-off, with flexibility on payment terms for discussion.

rebuttals.answer: You are right that the price has been stable, and we value that consistency. Stability ran both ways, though: across the same period we placed steady and growing volume with you, paid reliably and agreed each renewal with you on good terms. A flat price on a growing, predictable account is a fair result, not a hidden discount. Our aim is not a sharp cut. We want to keep this stability going for longer, with value coming through terms.

We accept that labour and rubber costs have risen and we have looked at both. Weighted by their share of this part's cost, they add only a little to the price. Material is a small part of the cost, so the stainless surcharge carries limited weight. Our own estimate of your plant cost also shows the current price leaves room to absorb these moves. That is why we see holding the current price as fair, rather than an increase.

Your quality and delivery record is excellent, and we say so gladly. That is exactly why we want a longer partnership with you. Nothing we propose touches the service level. A longer commitment and binding volume give you more planning room to keep it, not less. We also note that on-time delivery now sits just at the target, so steadier call-offs should help both sides.

We respect your head-office policy and will not ask you to break it. As we understand it, the freeze covers reductions, not increases. Your sales director also told us he was open on payment terms and call-off flexibility. We therefore propose to hold the current price through the freeze period and find the value in terms, which fits within your rules.

Congratulations on extending the approvals; we value them. That investment serves your wider market and opens new customers for you, so it should not be recovered from this single part. A longer agreement with growing volume from us helps you spread that cost over more pieces.

Fair point: our call-offs have not always been smooth, and the few rush orders are on us. Our forecast is shared with you, though, and it is rising. We are ready to turn it into a binding annual volume with a forecast-based monthly call-off plan. That removes most of the uncertainty you describe, and we would expect it to be reflected in the price over a longer term.

press: Under our framework agreement prices are fixed per calendar year, and since we received no change notice in the agreed period, we assume the current price continues for the coming year.
Our estimate of your plant cost suggests the current price already leaves a healthy margin to absorb this year's labour and rubber increases.
Since material is only a small share of this part's cost, we would weigh the steel and alloy headlines accordingly.
Given our rising forecast and your strong financial position, we see a longer fixed-price agreement with binding volume as a good result for both sides.
Our current payment term is already shorter than our standard, which we see as a contribution from our side to the overall package.
Your renewals in recent years have settled at an unchanged price, and we would like to continue that stability for a longer period.
